  "title": "administrator can see file names",
  "body": "There are some situations where a GL server may be administered by someone other than a receiver. In those instances, the receiver may not want the administrator to see meta data of leaks. The filenames are visible to an administrator via the files overview section.\r\n\r\nFilenames themselves can be revealing about the content within. In the most extreme conditions, can in of themselves give away the identity of a leaker that has not taken the right precautions. \r\n\r\nExample:\r\n`my_leak_by_alice_smith.pdf`\r\n\r\nFor a receiver this is of course ultimately an issue of trust with a leaker, however that same level of trust should not be automatically extended to the administrator for the following reasons:\r\n- an administrator can be 'coerced' into unlocking their admin panel\r\n- a GL server can be captured while logged into as administrator\r\n\r\nSo my proposal is to encrypt the file name with the receivers PGP key.",
